pharm: Semisynthetic podophyllotoxin; topoisomerase II inhibitor causing DNA strand breaks
summary: Etoposide (VP-16) is a semisynthetic podophyllotoxin and topoisomerase II inhibitor used, in combination with other agents, for refractory testicular tumors and as first-line therapy for small-cell lung cancer. It is given by IV infusion (or orally as capsules). Severe, dose-limiting myelosuppression with risk of infection or bleeding is the principal toxicity, and rapid IV infusion can cause hypotension. It must be given by clinicians experienced in cancer chemotherapy.
indications: Refractory testicular tumors, in combination, after appropriate surgery/chemo/radiotherapy
Small-cell lung cancer, first-line, in combination (injection and/or capsules)

dosage.d: 50-100 mg/m2/day on days 1-5, OR 100 mg/m2/day on days 1, 3 and 5
35 mg/m2/day for 4 days up to 50 mg/m2/day for 5 days
Roughly twice the IV dose, rounded to nearest 50 mg (e.g., 70 mg/m2/day x4 to 100 mg/m2/day x5)

admin: Administer by slow IV infusion over 30-60 minutes to avoid hypotension
Do not give by rapid IV injection
Avoid acrylic/ABS plastic devices with undiluted solution (cracking/leaking risk)
Use under supervision of a clinician experienced in cytotoxic therapy with marrow/supportive resources
Monitor blood pressure during infusion; handle as a hazardous drug
moa: Semisynthetic podophyllotoxin derivative that inhibits topoisomerase II, stabilizing the enzyme-DNA cleavage complex and producing DNA single- and double-strand breaks; arrests cells in late S/G2 phase.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to etoposide or podophyllotoxin derivatives
relative: Hepatic or renal impairment (consider dose reduction)

preg: Can cause fetal harm based on mechanism and animal data; avoid in pregnancy and advise effective contraception.
lact: Etoposide is present in human milk; discontinue breastfeeding during treatment and for a period afterward.
renal: Reduced clearance with renal impairment; give 75% of dose for CrCl 15-50 mL/min and individualize/monitor below that.
hepatic: Use with caution; reduced metabolism and low albumin increase free-drug exposure and toxicity. Consider dose reduction.

major: Other myelosuppressive chemotherapy / radiation — additive marrow suppression
Live vaccines — risk of severe/disseminated infection; avoid
moderate: Warfarin — elevated INR reported; monitor closely
Strong CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors — alter etoposide levels
interactions.food: Capsules may be taken with or without food.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor for tumor lysis (uric acid, electrolytes) at treatment start.

serious: Severe myelosuppression with infection or bleeding (dose-limiting)
Anaphylactic-type reactions (chills, fever, bronchospasm, dyspnea, hypotension)
Secondary acute leukemia (treatment-related, often with 11q23 abnormality)

monitoring: Complete blood count before and during each cycle (withhold for severe cytopenias)
counsel: Report fever, chills or any sign of infection at once
Hair loss is common and usually reversible
Use effective contraception during and after treatment; do not breastfeed
Tell staff immediately if you feel faint, flushed or short of breath during the infusion
pk: Cytotoxic over late S/G2 phase of cell cycle
Vials 20-25 C (68-77 F); capsules refrigerated 2-8 C per label
pearls: Boxed/principal warning: severe dose-limiting myelosuppression with infection or bleeding risk
Infuse over 30-60 minutes — rapid IV injection causes hypotension
Oral capsule dose is about twice the IV dose because bioavailability is roughly 50%
Reduce dose in renal impairment (75% for CrCl 15-50 mL/min)
Topoisomerase II inhibitors carry a risk of treatment-related secondary AML
missed: Doses are scheduled within a chemotherapy protocol and managed by the oncology team; missed or delayed doses are not self-administered.
overdose: No specific antidote. Overdose intensifies myelosuppression and mucositis; metabolic acidosis and hepatotoxicity reported at high doses. Provide intensive supportive care, transfusions, and management of infection.
